identity.title: What Limits Virtual Agent Application? OmniBench: A Scalable Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Essential Virtual Agent Capabilities

problem.claim: Develop scalable evaluation of multimodal virtual-agent capabilities across controllable, graph-structured tasks.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks reportedly have uncontrollable task complexity, extensive manual annotation requirements, and insufficient multidimensional evaluation.

contributions.claim: OmniBench is a self-generating graph-based benchmark whose pipeline synthesizes tasks with controllable complexity through subtask composition.
OmniEval evaluates virtual agents at the subtask and graph levels and tests 10 capabilities.
The authors provide 36k graph-structured tasks spanning 20 scenarios.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach through self-generating graph-based task synthesis and multidimensional graph-aware evaluation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The synthesized dataset reportedly achieved a 91% human acceptance rate.
The authors report that training on graph-structured data improves generalization across environments.
Multidimensional evaluations reportedly reveal virtual-agent performance across various capabilities.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLM-based virtual agents have shown strong performance, but current benchmarks have practical and evaluative limitations.
OmniBench addresses task-generation constraints with graph-based subtask composition and controllable complexity.
OmniEval adds subtask-level, graph-based, and 10-capability evaluation.
The authors report a 36k-task resource, 91% human acceptance, improved cross-environment generalization after training, and capability-level evaluations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a benchmark's task-generation mechanism with evaluation metrics designed for the same graph structure and reports dataset acceptance separately.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests making the unit of data construction explicit and matching evaluation granularity to it.
lessons.application: For a compositional benchmark, define primitive subtasks and composition rules, then report both primitive-level and whole-structure metrics.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when tasks are not naturally decomposable or when structure-specific metrics obscure the primary end-task objective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the environments, baselines, evaluation protocols, or statistical details supporting the reported generalization improvement.
The 91% human acceptance rate lacks annotation procedures, sample size, and acceptance criteria.
The abstract does not detail the 10 capabilities or the graph-based metrics.
